subject: Hugging is wrong, so why pull the hand this way?
alt: Satish Acharya’s two-panel cartoon. In the top panel, at left, a bearded young man in a white shirt and khaki trousers points with his finger and says: ‘WRONG!’. At right, an elderly white-bearded, bespectacled leader in a cream kurta and black jacket hugs a man in a blue shirt tightly; the elder wears an armband with the Israeli flag on his arm, and the man being hugged stares ahead, stunned. In the bottom panel, at left, the same elderly leader, in a blue vest, stands lost in thought with his hand on his chin. At right, the same young man grips with both hands the hands of a man in a black suit and red tie and pulls him towards himself; that man also wears an Israeli-flag armband. The speech balloon reads: ‘THIS WAY!’. The signature ‘SATISH ACHARYA’ is at the lower right.
chutki: In the top panel the young man calls one embrace ‘wrong’, one in which an arm carries an Israeli-flag armband. In the bottom panel the same young man takes both hands of a man with an Israeli-flag armband and says: ‘This way’, while the elderly leader watches with his hand on his chin.
The needle: the relationship called wrong in the top panel is the one being pulled towards in the bottom. Whether the objection is to the embrace or to who is embracing, the picture leaves unsaid.
